notes: syncEpoch line 29 genuinely uses `presetsRaw === this.lastPresetsRaw` reference identity; an in-place mutation of the same object is missed and a rebuilt equal object forces a full reparse. Latent contract issue; current caller passes the stable cartridge object so no active break, hence low.

findNextAvailableOrdinal throws at line 111 on exhaustion, and get()->allocateProcedural is on the resolve path, so an exhausted registry throws rather than degrading. Requires ~4^9 distinct procedural keys to reach, so realistically unreachable; real but low.

The `if (!this.exhaustionLogged)` block (lines 37-39) only sets the flag with no logging inside; console.warn at lines 40-43 sits after it and fires unconditionally on every get() once exhausted. Dead store plus per-call warn spam, exactly as claimed.

resolveTickEntity returns `{...entity, __attentionLightSuppressed:true}` (lines 20-24), a fresh object per tick for each non-focused entity during focus, breaking any reference-identity cache and allocating per frame. Real; impact bounded to focus periods, so low.

syncFullRebuild uses `entity.id ?? ''` as the records map key (line 56); two id-less entities collide on '' and overwrite each other so only one gets a visual instance. Real wrong behavior, contingent on id-less entities existing.

The incremental branch (line 90) only runs when !fullRebuild and mutationRevision is then overwritten, but syncFullRebuild reprocesses ALL entities, so a full rebuild genuinely supersedes per-entity mutations. The unstated assumption holds; immaterial.

assertAvatarAppearance (AvatarTextureSupport.ts:60-63) checks only appearanceKey; getAvatarPart throws on out-of-range index (line 24). A keyed-but-corrupt appearance with a bad shape index throws inside texture generation rather than at the guard, as claimed.

The dispatcher has four explicit `if (event.kind === ...)` cases then falls through to spawnSmokePuff (lines 63-70) with event.x/y/radius; any new/unknown kind or one lacking those fields spawns an unintended puff at undefined coords. Real latent fragility; low as no such kind exists today.

resolveNervousDeliveredRate returns 0 (line 17); veinFlowProjection sets nervous edges' deliveredRate to it (line 41) and veinsDisplayBuilder computes blobSpawnRateHz = deliveredRate/energy_per_blob (line 64), so nervous flow never animates. Real; may be intentional-placeholder, cosmetic, hence low.

widthPx = resolveBaseWidth(...) at line 36 is unconditionally overwritten for both edge kinds (lines 37-41), and VeinEdgeKind is exactly 'resource-demand'|'nervous' (types.ts:2), so the base-width call can never affect output. Dead computation with a live-looking doc comment.

grep confirms resolveDemandWidth, resolvePulsedWidth, groupEdges, resolveOffsetStep and colorUtils resolveVeinColor have no references outside their own definition files (not even tests). Dead exports carrying authoritative-sounding comments, as claimed.

projectVeinEdgeFlow calls resolveTerminalChainTargetId per resource-demand edge, and each call scans forward via findNextEdgeIndex (line 8) per hop, giving O(n^2) over edges each frame. Real but small-graph-bounded, so low.

scene.events.on('update', update) at line 27 is never matched by an .off in destroyPointerSceneSystems (lines 31-37), which only destroys controller/preview and deletes the WeakMap entry. The closure stays subscribed holding the destroyed preview; on scene-instance reuse it fires preview.update() on torn-down state.

grep confirms resolveBodyAvatarExportInputs is imported only by its own .test.ts; the live avatar path uses buildBodyAvatarImageRequest. Dead production code duplicating spec/seed/appearance resolution with a maintained test for an unreachable path, as claimed.

The file imports vitest (line 2) and is not named *.test.ts, but grep shows it is imported only by test files; nothing in the product graph references it, so the bundler never pulls vitest into a production build. A naming/hygiene latency, not an active defect.

resolveDragReleaseUpdate returns { bodyId, ownerId } on accept (line 43) with no expectedCurrentOwnerId, while the restore path pins expectedCurrentOwnerId:'sys_pointer' (line 48). If sys_pointer ownership changed between pickup and release the accept applies with no concurrency guard. Real but narrow.

previousSnapshot (line 16) and veinsSystem.graph.edges (line 17) are read through `as any`, so a rename silently degrades to false/0 with no compile error. Debug-panel only, so low; the reach-in would misreport health without signal, as claimed.

parseBackgroundConfig uses BackgroundConfigSchema.parse (line 14, throws), called from refreshConfig->update every frame (BiologicalFogBackground.ts:22,70) with no try/catch. Schema enforces intensity>=0 and threshold_low<threshold_high (background.ts superRefine), and the camera path uses safeParse; a malformed background config throws the frame loop.

base_color/lift_color are z.string().default(...) with no hex validation (background.ts:29-30), yet normalizeHexColor throws 'Invalid biological fog color' on non-hex (line 36), and it runs per frame in BiologicalFogBackground.update (line 32). A value like 'purple' passes config parse then hard-fails the render loop.

Module-global cache (line 9) is only written (line 29) and read (line 26), never cleared or bounded; BodyAvatarPresentation holds three data-URL strings (bodyAvatarBridge.ts). Each new appearanceKey adds a permanent entry, leaking monotonically over re-rolled seeds. Slow leak, so low.

The shader is GLSL ES 1.00 (precision/varying/gl_FragColor at lines 2,20,56) and declares `vec2 smooth` (line 29); `smooth` is a reserved interpolation qualifier in ES 1.00, so strict WebGL1 drivers reject it and the fog silently never renders. Works on permissive drivers (ANGLE); cosmetic + driver-dependent, hence low.

bindInput() calls scene.input.addPointer(1) when fewer than 2 pointers exist (line 81), but destroy() only toggles handlers off (line 115) and never releases the added pointer. Repeated create/destroy cycles accrete pointers on the shared input plugin, as claimed.

tickInstanceSafe wraps instance.tick in try/catch that only console.errors and swallows (lines 37-42). A module throwing mid-tick is silently skipped every frame, so a persistently broken display renders nothing/stale while the frame loop keeps running as healthy.

validateScratchSlots collects leaked scratch objects and only console.errors them (lines 72-77); it neither destroys nor clears them, and releaseAnchors releases the anchors regardless. A genuine leak is surfaced only as a log, not remediated. Detected (not fully silent) and diagnostic-only, so low.

setInstanceInteractionBlocked reaches line 34 (target.disableInteractive?.()) only when target.input is falsy (line 30 returns otherwise); a target with no input is not interactive to begin with, so the optional-chain no-op cannot leave a blockable entity interactive. Immaterial.

resolveVeinsPreset calls resolveHeartbeatPreset (line 29) with no try/catch; heartbeatRules.ts calls adapter.evaluate (line 31) which runs compileExpression + jsonLogic.apply (JsonLogicAdapter.ts:25,42), both able to throw on a malformed operator-authored rule. The exception then propagates through VeinsSystem.update every frame instead of degrading to default.

spawnGoldRings releases the pooled ring only in the tween onComplete (lines 85-88); the tween handle (line 77) is discarded with no cancellation hook. If the scene/tween manager is torn down before completion, onComplete never runs and the ring is never released to the pool. Real across teardown, benign steady-state.

spawnSmokePuff schedules emitter.destroy() via scene.time.delayedCall(420, ...) (line 117) and ignores the timer handle; on abrupt teardown before 420ms the emitter may be left undestroyed. Largely covered by Phaser's normal scene child/timer cleanup, so low.

The per-source loop uses a bare `catch { continue; }` (lines 111-116) with no logging or reason comment, so a genuinely malformed asset that throws for every source is indistinguishable from a legitimately-absent key; both yield a silent null and missing icon. Cosmetic impact, so low.

Same defect as P.run1.115 from the fire-and-forget angle: the 'update' listener attached at line 27 is never detached in destroyPointerSceneSystems (lines 31-37), so the subscription outlives the systems it drives, retaining the destroyed preview and invoking preview.update() on torn-down state under scene reuse.

drawPlaceholder returns false when the variant or texture source is missing (lines 56,58) else true (line 65); at line 116 the caller discards it, so a missing placeholder texture draws nothing and the render returns a blank data-URL (line 117) with no error or fallback. Cosmetic empty-icon, so low.

The try (lines 18-33) wraps registry resolution, seed resolution and buildBodyAvatarPresentation (which throws on a missing 2d context) and the catch bare-returns null with zero logging and no pdd-ignore marker. Any genuine defect there silently renders no avatar with no diagnostics.

store() swallows localStorage.setItem failures with an empty catch (line 22); this is a debug-toggle persistence best-effort that cannot affect product behavior, only whether the debug flag persists. Style/hygiene (unmarked swallow) only, immaterial.

readStored() catches localStorage access errors and defaults to false (lines 6-8), a reasonable debug-only fallback the finding itself calls benign; only the missing pdd-ignore reason comment distinguishes it. Immaterial to product behavior.
